title: Global dashboard keyboard flow, dynamic contrast, and locale-ready axes — prototype review
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Prototype and review for keyboard-first interactions and accessibility readiness across the Redwood Console dashboard panels (rollouts, cost heatmap, and per-model throughput charts). Focus areas: 1) deterministic keyboard flow across multi-pane dashboards including splitter and modal dialogs; 2) dynamic color-contrast tuning for heatmaps and alert badges that adapts to light/dark themes and user contrast preferences; 3) locale-aware axis formatting and RTL mirroring for scrubbers and timeline controls. Deliverables: annotated Figma prototype, ARIA spec sheet for engineers, and a short test script for accessibility QA in English, Spanish, and Japanese locales.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard navigation: Tab/Shift+Tab, Arrow keys, Home/End navigate panes, charts, and scrubber without trapping; focus order documented in ARIA flow chart
Screen reader semantics: Chart interactive regions expose labels and current value on focus; scrubber announces timestamp in locale-aware format
Contrast thresholds: Heatmap and status badges meet WCAG AA for normal text and 3:1 for UI components where applicable; color tokens include fallback patterns when data overlay reduces contrast
RTL support: Timeline scrubber mirrors correctly, axis labels align and number formatting uses locale rules; no overlaps when translated strings are longer
Prototype artifacts: Figma links and export showing keyboard-focus states, and an ARIA attribute table included for each interactive element
design_notes: Use semantic DOM order for charts so keyboard focus flows naturally without JS reordering; visual layout can be achieved with CSS grid and 'order' only for presentation where necessary
Implemented a dynamic overlay layer that adjusts heatmap palette based on computed luminance of background to preserve contrast; alternative textures considered for colorblind users
For large locale label expansion, axis label compression uses 'collapsed' mode with accessible tooltip on focus rather than truncation with ellipsis only
Splitter control receives a 2px focus ring and an expanded hit target on keyboard focus to meet touch and keyboard affordance requirements
Decided against separate keyboard-only control set to reduce cognitive overhead; instead enhanced existing controls to be fully keyboard operable
decisions: Adopt ICU number and date formatting for axis labels and scrubber announcements to ensure correct thousands separators and month order per locale
Provide two contrast palettes: 'data-first' and 'ui-first'. Default is 'data-first' for dense heatmaps but will toggle to 'ui-first' when contrast delta falls below threshold
ARIA: charts will expose role=region with aria-labelledby pointing to chart title and role=slider for scrubber with aria-valuetext reporting localized timestamp
Fallback: when browser locale not supported, use English formatting but label UI with user locale to avoid silent changes
open_questions: Should the scrubber announce both UTC and localized time on first focus for globally distributed customers? Trade-off: verbosity vs clarity
Do engineering constraints on existing chart library allow adding role=slider behavior, or do we need a lightweight wrapper component? ENG-4821 to confirm
How should we expose contrast toggles in the UI? Small toggle in settings or an automatic adaptive banner when contrast problems are detected?
Is there a minimum translation length budget per axis label that would trigger label collapse? Need PM input for acceptable truncation behavior
tasks: Finalize Figma prototype with keyboard interactions and export interactive HTML snippets (Mariana)
